text: I’ll model the requested air region as a thin swept helical duct, not the surrounding solids. Because the thread flank angle and crest/root widths are unspecified, I’ll use an assumed symmetric 30° trapezoidal thread profile and make the leakage ribbon 0.2 mm thick normal to the mating flank. The six-turn path will run over the stated 12 mm engagement. I’ll first inspect the installed CAD sweep/helix API, then create and render a deliberately coarse solid.

The coarse CAD solid will use metres from the outset. I’ll place a \(0.2\) mm by \(1/\cos(15^\circ)=1.035\) mm section on a 19.5 mm mean-radius helix; the latter is the midpoint of the stated 20 mm crest and 19 mm root radii. The 30° included flank angle and this rectangularized flank-width interpretation are assumptions necessitated by the missing profile widths.

The sweep is a valid solid with the expected six turns and small cross-section. I’ll now render it from an oblique view to verify that the path is continuous and that the end sections are exposed only at the two helix termini.

The preview confirms a continuous open-ended six-turn ribbon with no overlap between turns. I’ll now create the four named boundary groups directly from the helical coordinates. To close the rectangular leakage section without inventing extra patch names, the two “lower/inner” longitudinal faces will be grouped as `neck_flank`, and the two opposing “upper/outer” faces as `lid_flank`; the terminal cross-sections are `inner_end` and `outer_end`. The STL tessellation will also become the exact boundary of the structured volume mesh.

I’ll convert this same parameter grid into a conformal hexahedral mesh: 720 stations along the helix (120 per turn), 2 cells across the 0.2 mm gap, and 8 across the modeled flank span, for 11,520 cells. This keeps the thin direction resolved while remaining modest enough for a first OpenFOAM mesh.

Conversion produced the expected 11,520 all-hexahedral cells and all four named physical groups. The converter’s generic “undefined faces” message can occur while it assembles the boundary, so I’ll inspect the resulting patch counts and run the binding `checkMesh` rather than assume it is harmless.

`checkMesh` exited before reporting topology, so I need the untruncated diagnostic. I’ll inspect the end of the combined log to identify whether this is a mesh-read issue or a geometric-quality failure.

The mesh itself was not read because this OpenFOAM build requires minimal `fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` dictionaries even for the extended check. I’ll add empty valid dictionaries and rerun the full check.

The utility requires the standard scheme subdictionaries rather than a truly empty file. I’ll supply inert defaults sufficient for mesh inspection only; no fields or boundary conditions are being created.

The full topology and geometry check now passes: one region, closed boundary, 11,520 hexahedra, maximum non-orthogonality \(0.022^\circ\), maximum skewness 0.066, and aspect ratio 7.37. I’ll make a final visual inspection of the actual OpenFOAM boundary, colored by its four patch names, rather than relying only on the CAD preview.

The converted boundary contains exactly the requested four patch datasets. I’ll render them with distinct colors and mesh edges; the terminal patches are small by design because each is only the \(0.2\) mm by \(1.035\) mm channel cross-section.

The final view confirms the alternating solid-contact patches and the two exposed helical termini. Before declaring completion, I’ll independently weld the four exported STLs and count free/non-manifold edges, ensuring the separate patch files form one closed leakage-volume surface when combined.

Completed the helical air-channel geometry and OpenFOAM mesh.

- Geometry: single-start, six-turn helical leakage ribbon over 12 mm at 2 mm pitch.
- Measured gap: 0.200 mm.
- Thread basis: 40 mm neck OD, 1 mm depth, giving an assumed 39 mm mean path diameter.
- Mesh: 11,520 structured hexahedra; one connected region.
- Patches: `neck_flank`, `lid_flank`, `inner_end`, `outer_end`.
- Exported exactly one STL per patch under `constant/triSurface`; their welded union has zero free/non-manifold edges.
- `checkMesh -allGeometry -allTopology`: **Mesh OK**. Maximum non-orthogonality 0.022°, skewness 0.066, aspect ratio 7.37.

Assumptions due to unspecified thread-profile details: symmetric 30° included trapezoidal flank angle; modeled flank span 1.035 mm; the two lower/inner longitudinal channel faces are grouped as neck contact and the opposing two as lid contact. No flow solution or boundary conditions were created.
